Post-infectious irritable bowel syndrome, diarrhea-predominant (PI-IBS-D)

The antecedent camping exposure with illness in a close contact is epidemiologically consistent with a prior enteric infection — a well-established trigger for PI-IBS, which accounts for ~10% of new IBS cases and commonly follows even subclinical infections. Critically, the summary contains *no physical exam findings*, not even confirmation of normality — the DRE was performed but its result is *not documented*, so it provides zero diagnostic information and must be treated as unknown. Thus, the diagnosis must rest solely on the positive clinical criteria and absence of red flags — aligning precisely with PI-IBS-D.
